titleEn: The Glory of Kings — Makeda on Wisdom as a Sea, and Her Ban on Sorcery (ch. 89)
part: ch. 89 — Makeda on Wisdom as a Sea, and Her Ban on Sorcery
about: Makeda answers the Israelites’ plea of the previous chapter: she will not treat them as servants but honour them as fathers and teachers, and she bids them teach the people. She speaks of the water of knowledge she has not yet drunk to the full, prays in a long run of petitions that wisdom may hold her fast, and tells how she dived into the sea for wisdom’s treasures, for her people and the nations around. She tells the lords that God has given them a seed in Zion and a dwelling-place among them, charges them to love justice and give up their old practices, sorcery among them, on pain of plunder, and bids Azariah tell of Zion’s love for the heavenly king.

sentences.t: ፹፱ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ነገረቶሙ ፡ ንግሥት ፡ ለደቂቀ ፡ እስራኤል ።
sentences.l: 89. Where told-them queen to-children-of Israel.
sentences.i: Chapter 89: How the queen spoke to the children of Israel.
sentences.n: Chapter heading, a unit of its own, built like the heading of ch. 88: ኀበ opens a title-like clause, ‘how’ rather than ‘where’ (?). ነገረቶሙ is ነገረ ‘speak, tell’ in the 3fs perfect (-ት) with -ሙ ‘them’; the object is then repeated by ለደቂቀ እስራኤል ‘to the children of Israel’ (ለ- + ደቂቅ in the construct state ‘children-of’ + the name), the doubling Geʿez likes.

sentences.t: ወአውሥአት ፡ ንግሥት ፡ ወትቤሎሙ ፡ አኮ ፡ ከመ ፡ አግብርት ፡ ዘትብሉ ፡ አላ ፡ ንሬስየክሙ ፡ ከመ ፡ አብ ፡ ወከመ ፡ መምህር ፤
sentences.l: And-answered-she queen and-said-she-to-them: not as servants what-you-say, but we-make-you as father and-as teacher;
sentences.i: And the queen answered and said to them, ‘It is not as servants, as you say, but we regard you as a father and as a teacher;
sentences.n: ወአውሥአት ‘and she answered’ (ወ- + causative አውሥአ, 3fs perfect), then ወትቤሎሙ ‘and she said to them’ (ትቤ, 3fs of the defective verb ‘say’, + ሎሙ). አኮ is the negative ‘it is not’. ዘትብሉ ‘what you say’ (ዘ- + 2mp imperfect of ብህለ) answers the plea at the end of ch. 88, ‘make us as your servants’. ንሬስየክሙ is ረሰየ ‘make, set, treat as’ in the 1cp imperfect with -ክሙ ‘you’; I take it as a plain present ‘we regard/make you’ (it could be a wish, ‘let us make you’). ወከመ ‘and as’ repeats ከመ ‘as’. The direct speech opens here and runs to the ፨ that ends unit 24; the last unit is narrative again.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ አንትሙ ፡ ዐቃብያነ ፡ ሕጉ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወመራሕያነ ፡ ትእዛዙ ፡ ለአምላከ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ወሰብአ ፡ ቤቱ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወዐቃብያኒሃ ፡ ለጽዮን ፡ ታቦተ ፡ ሕጉ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወአልቦ ፡ ዘንትዐደው ፡ እምትእዛዝክሙ ፡ እስመ ፡ አንትሙ ፡ ትከውኑነ ፡ መርሐ ፡ በኀበ ፡ ፍኖተ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ እምኵሉ ፡ እኩይ ፤
sentences.l: for you guardians-of law-his of-God and-guides-of command-his of-God-of Israel and-men-of house-his of-God and-guardians-her of-Zion ark-of law-his of-God, and-there-is-not that-we-transgress from-your-command; for you will-be-for-us guide in-presence-of way-of God from-all evil;
sentences.i: for you are the keepers of the law of God and the guides of the commandment of the God of Israel, the people of God’s house and the keepers of Zion, the ark of the law of God; and there is nothing that we would transgress (?) from your commandment, for you will be a guide for us on the way of God, away from all evil;
sentences.n: A string of construct chains: ዐቃብያነ ሕጉ ለእግዚኣብሔር ‘keepers-of his-law of-God’ (the owner is named after the suffix, ሕጉ … ለእግዚኣብሔር, as elsewhere), ወመራሕያነ ትእዛዙ ‘guides-of his command’, ወሰብአ ቤቱ ‘men-of his house’ (rendered ‘people of his house’, as in ch. 88). ወዐቃብያኒሃ ለጽዮን ‘and her keepers, of Zion’, then ታቦተ ሕጉ ‘ark-of his law’ in apposition: Zion is the Ark, the central claim of the book. ዘንትዐደው ‘that we transgress’ (ዘ- + tä-stem ተዐደወ); the relative ዘ- with a first-person verb is loose, ‘nothing that we transgress’, and I give it with (?). ትከውኑነ ‘you will be for us’ (2mp imperfect + -ነ). በኀበ ‘in the presence of’ here is uncertain (?); I take መርሐ በኀበ ፍኖተ እግዚኣብሔር as ‘a guide on/at the way of God’. እምኵሉ እኩይ ‘from all evil’ gives the direction ‘away from’.

sentences.t: ንትገሐሥ ፡ በቃልክሙ ፡ እምዘኢይሠምር ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወንቅረብ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ሠናይ ፡ ዘሠምረ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ በትእዛዘ ፡ ዚአክሙ ፤
sentences.l: let-us-turn-aside by-your-word from-that-not he-is-pleased God, and-let-us-draw-near to all good that he-was-pleased God in-command your;
sentences.i: let us turn aside, at your word, from what God does not favour, and draw near to all the good that God has favoured by your commandment;
sentences.n: ንትገሐሥ is the tä-stem of ገሐሠ, 1cp jussive, ‘let us turn aside’; it is the verb of ኢትትገሐሥ ‘do not turn aside’ in the queen’s charge to her son (ch. 88), and its perfect ተግሕሠ comes a few units on, ‘if he turned aside from the way of God’; I keep ‘turn aside’ in all three. እምዘኢይሠምር ‘from that which he is not pleased with’ (እም- + ዘ- + ኢ- + ሠምረ ‘be pleased, favour’); then ዘሠምረ in the perfect, ‘which he was pleased with’. ወንቅረብ ‘and let us draw near’ (1cp). Both verbs are jussive in sense.

sentences.t: ወባሕቱ ፡ አይድዑ ፡ ለዝንቱ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ሕዝብ ፡ ወመሀርዎሙ ፡ ቃላተ ፡ አእምሮ ፡ እስመ ፡ አልቦ ፡ አመ ፡ ሰምዑ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ዮም ፡ ዘከመዝ ፤
sentences.l: But proclaim to-this all people and-teach-them words-of knowledge, for there-is-not when they-heard without today such;
sentences.i: But proclaim it to all this people and teach them words of knowledge, for they have never heard the like until today;
sentences.n: አይድዑ is a causative imperative (2mp, ‘make known, proclaim’; the root, ይድዐ, I give from memory and hold loosely (?)). ለዝንቱ ኵሉ ሕዝብ ‘to this whole people’. ወመሀርዎሙ ‘and teach them’ (መሀረ + -ሙ). ቃላተ አእምሮ ‘words of knowledge’; አእምሮ, ‘knowing, knowledge’, is the key word of the chapter and I keep ‘knowledge’ for it throughout, leaving ‘understanding’ for ልቡና. አልቦ አመ ሰምዑ … ‘there is no time they heard … ’, i.e. they never heard; ዘእንበለ ዮም ‘except/before today’; ዘከመዝ ‘such a thing’.

sentences.t: ወባሕቱ ፡ ጥበብሰ ፡ ወአእምሮ ፡ ታበርህ ፡ ከመ ፡ ብርሃነፀሐይ ፡ ለእለ ፡ ቦሙ ፡ አእምሮ ።
sentences.l: But wisdom-indeed and-knowledge she-shines like light-of-sun to-those who in-them knowledge.
sentences.i: Yet wisdom and knowledge shine like the light of the sun on those who have knowledge.
sentences.n: ጥበብሰ has the contrastive -ሰ: ‘as for wisdom’. The verb ታበርህ is feminine (አብርሀ, ‘make bright, shine’), agreeing with ጥበብ ‘wisdom’, which is feminine, and which the speaker will call ‘her’ from here on. ብርሃነፀሐይ is printed as one word, ‘light-of-sun’ (ብርሃን in the construct + ፀሐይ); a source slip for ብርሃነ ፡ ፀሐይ, kept as printed. ለእለ ቦሙ አእምሮ ‘to those who have knowledge’ (ቦሙ ‘in them’, the Geʿez way of saying ‘have’).

sentences.t: ወአንሰ ፡ እስከ ፡ ይእዜሂ ፡ ኢረወይክዎ ፡ ለማየ ፡ አእምሮ ፡ እስመ ፡ ይጥዕም ፡ እምነ ፡ መዓር ፡ ወያረዊ ፡ እምነ ፡ ወይን ፡ ወያጸግብ ፡ ወያጐሥዕ ፡ ጥበበ ፡ ወያስዖዝዝ ፡ ልቡና ፡ ወያልሕስ ፡ ከመ ፡ ዘሰክረ ፡ ወያለጸልጽ ፡ ከመ ፡ ዘጐየ ፡ ወያሀ ፡ ፉ ፡ ከመ ፡ ዘጾረ ፡ ክቡደ ፡ በፍኖተ ፡ ዐቀብ ፡ በብሔረ ፡ ሐሩር ፡ ወላህበ ፡ ፀሐይ ፤
sentences.l: And-as-for-me until now-even not-I-have-drunk-my-fill-of-it of-water-of knowledge, for it-is-sweet than honey and-it-quenches than wine and-it-satisfies and-it-fills (?) wisdom and-it-bewilders (?) understanding and-it-weakens (?) like one-who got-drunk and-it-makes-falter (?) like one-who ran and-ያሀ ፉ (?) like one-who bore heavy on-path-of steep (?) in-land-of heat and-flame-of sun;
sentences.i: As for me, I have not yet drunk my fill of the water of knowledge, for it is sweeter than honey, and more quenching than wine; it satisfies and fills (?) with wisdom, it bewilders (?) the understanding, it leaves one weak (?) as a man who is drunk, and faltering (?) as one who has been running, and ያሀ ፉ (?) as one who carries a heavy load on a steep (?) path in a land of heat and the blaze of the sun;
sentences.n: Here the speech turns to the metaphor of the ‘water of knowledge’ (ማየ አእምሮ), which she has not yet drunk to the full (ኢረወይክዎ, ረወየ ‘drink one’s fill’, 1cs perfect + -ዎ ‘it’). ይጥዕም እምነ መዓር ‘is sweet more than honey’ (እምነ before a noun gives the comparative); ወያረዊ ‘and quenches’ (causative). Then a run of verbs whose roots I cannot check without Dillmann, so all of them are hedged: ያጐሥዕ (‘fills’? the root ጐሥዐ is otherwise ‘push, strike’ in my memory), ያስዖዝዝ (‘bewilders’), ያልሕስ (‘weakens’), ያለጸልጽ (‘makes falter’); the sense is plain, that this water overwhelms like drink or labour. ወያሀ ፡ ፉ is printed with a stray space (perhaps one word ያሀፉ); I keep the two pieces as printed and cannot place them (perhaps ‘pants’ (?)). ከመ ዘሰክረ ‘like one who got drunk’ (ከመ ዘ- + perfect). ፍኖተ ዐቀብ ‘a path of ʿäqäb’, taken as ‘steep, slope’ (?). ላህበ ፀሐይ ‘flame of the sun’. ‘Heat’ here is ሐሩር, so the picture is a desert march.

sentences.t: ሶበ ፡ ተከሥተ ፡ አልባቢሆሙ ፡ ለጠቢባን ፡ ለትንቢት ፡ ወለምህሮ ፡ ኢይፈርህዎ ፡ ለንጉሥ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ዕበየ ፡ ክብሩ ፡ ለእመ ፡ ተግሕሠ ፡ እምፍኖተ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ።
sentences.l: When was-opened their-hearts to-the-wise for-prophecy and-for-teaching, not-they-fear the-king because-of greatness-of his-glory if he-withdrew from-way-of God.
sentences.i: When the hearts of the wise are opened to prophecy and teaching, they do not fear a king on account of the greatness of his glory, if he has turned away from the way of God.
sentences.n: ተከሥተ ‘was opened’ is a singular verb with the plural ‘hearts’ (አልባቢሆሙ, ‘their hearts’); the pattern is common. ለጠቢባን ‘to the wise’ (ጠቢብ, plural). ለትንቢት ወለምህሮ ‘for prophecy and for teaching’ (ምህሮ is the verbal noun of መሀረ). ኢይፈርህዎ ለንጉሥ ‘they do not fear the king’; the ለ- marks the object and is doubled by -ዎ ‘him’. በእንተ ዕበየ ክብሩ ‘because of the greatness of his glory’; ዕበይ is in the construct. ለእመ ‘if’ introduces the condition; ተግሕሠ as above (?). The point, for the Israelites and for her son the king, is that wisdom is free to rebuke a king who strays.

sentences.t: ነዋኬዝ ፡ ዘተነግረ ፡ ቃለ ፡ ሕግ ፡ ዘበአማን ፡ አእምሮ ፡ ለእለ ፡ ይፈቅድዎ ፡ ወይሰትይዎ ፡ ወይረውይዎ ፤
sentences.l: Behold (?) what was-told: word-of law, truly knowledge, to-those who they-desire-it and-they-drink-it and-they-drink-their-fill-of-it;
sentences.i: Behold, what has been said is the word of the law, in truth knowledge, for those who desire it, and drink it, and drink their fill of it;
sentences.n: ነዋኬዝ is one word as printed, ነዋ ‘behold’ + a particle I take to be ከዝ ‘here, now’ (?). ዘተነግረ ‘what was said’ (ዘ- + tä-stem passive of ነገረ). ቃለ ሕግ ‘word of law’ is a construct; ዘበአማን ‘truly’ (‘of truth’). The three verbs of desiring and drinking take -ዎ ‘it’ and continue the water image: ይፈቅድዎ, ይሰትይዎ, ይረውይዎ (the last is the same ረወየ ‘drink one’s fill’ as in the ‘water of knowledge’ unit).

sentences.t: አንሰ ፡ እጼሊ ፡ እግዚኦ ፡ አምላከ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ቅዱሰ ፡ ቅዱሳን ፡ ሀበኒ ፡ ከመ ፡ እትልዋ ፡ ለጥበብ ፡ ወኢይትገደፍ ፡ ሀበኒ ፡ ከመ ፡ እጠቀም ፡ ባቲ ፡ ወኢይንኀል ፡ ሀበኒ ፡ ከመ ፡ እሣረር ፡ ባቲ ፡ ወኢያንቀልቅል ፡ ሀበኒ ፡ ከመ ፡ እትዐመድ ፡ ባቲ ፡ ወኢይጽነን ፡ ሀበኒ ፡ ከመ ፡ እሰወር ፡ ባቲ ፡ ወኢይትቀላዕ ፡ ሀበኒ ፡ ከመ ፡ እትሐነጽ ፡ ባቲ ፡ ወኢይንሐድ ፡
sentences.l: As-for-me I-pray O-Lord God-of Israel holy-one-of holy-ones: give-me that I-follow wisdom and-not he-is-cast-off; give-me that I-profit in-her and-not he-grows-slack (?); give-me that I-take-root (?) in-her and-not he-shakes; give-me that I-lean in-her and-not he-gives-way (?); give-me that I-am-sheltered (?) in-her and-not he-is-torn-away (?); give-me that I-am-built in-her and-not he-departs (?);
sentences.i: As for me, I pray, O Lord, God of Israel, Holy One of holy ones: grant me to follow wisdom and not be cast aside; grant me to profit by her and not grow slack (?); grant me to take root (?) in her and not be shaken; grant me to lean on her and not give way (?); grant me to be sheltered (?) in her and not be torn away (?); grant me to be built up in her and not depart (?);
sentences.n: The prayer opens a long run of petitions of one pattern, ሀበኒ ከመ [1cs imperfect] ባቲ ወኢ[3ms verb] ‘give me that I [do so-and-so] in her, and [may it] not …’. ሀበኒ is the imperative of ወሀበ + -ኒ ‘me’; ከመ + the 1cs imperfect gives the purpose; ባቲ is በ- ‘in, by’ + -ቲ ‘her’, wisdom (ጥበብ, feminine). I render ባቲ ‘in her’ or ‘by her’ and the ወኢ- clause as an infinitive, ‘and not be …’. The grammar of that clause is odd: the verbs are 3ms (ይትገደፍ ‘he/it is cast off’) with no stated subject, although the sense seems to be ‘and that I not …’; I keep the 3ms in `l` and ‘not be …’ in the English. The verbs are mostly ones I can only guess at without Dillmann: እጠቀም ‘profit’ (ጠቀመ), ይንኀል ‘grow slack’ (?), ይንሐድ ‘depart’ (?), እሣረር ‘take root’ (ሠረረ, ‘be firm, rooted’ (?)), ያንቀልቅል ‘shake’, እትዐመድ ‘lean’ (ዐምድ ‘pillar’), ይጽነን ‘give way’ (?), እሰወር ‘be hidden/sheltered’ (?), ይትቀላዕ ‘be torn away’ (?), እትሐነጽ ‘be built’. እግዚኦ is the vocative ‘O Lord’; ቅዱሰ ቅዱሳን ‘holy one of holy ones’, a title of God (the masculine ቅዱስ, not the place ቅድስተ ቅዱሳን ‘Holy of Holies’). This unit and the next two are one unpunctuated stretch in the source (no ። or ፤ until ወኢይተፍኣ ፤), about 79 words; I have cut it at the end of ወኢይንሐድ and at ባቲ before በስንኣሃ, so that no single unit passes 45 words.

sentences.t: ሀበኒ ፡ ከመ ፡ እትወርዘው ፡ ባቲ ፡ ወኢይድክም ፡ ሀበኒ ፡ ከመ ፡ እቁም ፡ ባቲ ፡ ወኢይደቅ ፡ ሀበኒ ፡ ከመ ፡ እትመርጐዝ ፡ ባቲ ፡ ወኢይተንትን ፡ ሀበኒ ፡ ከመ ፡ እሠአን ፡ ባቲ ፡ ወኢይድኀፅ ፡ ሀበኒ ፡ ከመ ፡ እትአኀዝ ፡ ባቲ ፡ ወኢይሰጠም ፡ ሀበኒ ፡ ከመ ፡ እጽናዕ ፡ ባቲ ፡ ወኢይሠረም ፡ ሀበኒ ፡ ከመ ፡ እንበር ፡ ባቲ ፡
sentences.l: give-me that I-leap (?) in-her and-not he-grows-weary; give-me that I-stand in-her and-not he-falls; give-me that I-lean-on-staff in-her and-not he-staggers; give-me that I-am-shod (?) in-her and-not he-lags-behind (?); give-me that I-hold-fast in-her and-not he-sinks; give-me that I-am-firm in-her and-not he-is-torn (?); give-me that I-abide in-her;
sentences.i: grant me to leap (?) in her and not grow weary; grant me to stand in her and not fall; grant me to lean on a staff in her and not stagger; grant me to be shod (?) in her and not lag behind (?); grant me to hold fast to her and not sink; grant me to be firm in her and not be torn (?); grant me to abide in her;
sentences.n: The petitions continue in the same pattern; the unit begins at ሀበኒ because the ወኢ- clause belongs to the petition before it. Pairs: እትወርዘው ‘leap, spring’ (?) / ይድክም ‘grow weary’; እቁም ‘stand’ / ይደቅ ‘fall’; እትመርጐዝ ‘lean on a staff’ (መርጐዝ ‘staff’) / ይተንትን ‘stagger, totter’; እሠአን ‘be shod’ (from ሠአን ‘sandal’ (?)) / ይድኀፅ ‘lag behind’ (?); እትአኀዝ ‘hold fast’ / ይሰጠም ‘sink’ (the sinking prepares the diving image); እጽናዕ ‘be firm’ / ይሠረም ‘be torn’ (?). The last petition, እንበር ባቲ ‘that I abide in her’ (ነበረ), has no ወኢ- clause and ends the series. The picture is a traveller: stand, staff, sandals, grip, foothold.

sentences.t: በስንኣሃ ፡ እጽገብ ፡ በማእዳ ፡ ወኢይሜጽራ ፡ እስትያ ፡ ወኢይረውያ ፡ እጽገባ ፡ ወኢይተፍኣ ፤
sentences.l: in-her-ስንኣ I-am-satisfied at-her-table, and-not-he-ሜጽራ (?) my-drinking-her, and-not-he-drinks-his-fill-of-her (?) my-being-filled-her, and-not-he-spits-her-out;
sentences.i: by her ስንኣ (?) I am satisfied at her table; may drinking her not ሜጽራ (?), may my being filled with her not glut (?), and may she not be spat out.
sentences.n: በስንኣሃ is በ- + ስንኣ (?) + -ሃ ‘her’; I do not know ስንኣ (perhaps ‘bounty, sweetness’ (?)). በማእዳ ‘at her table’ (ማእድ). እጽገብ ‘I am satisfied’ (ጸገበ, as in ያጸግብ in the ‘water of knowledge’ unit). Then three more ወኢ- clauses with 3ms verbs and ‘her’: ወኢይሜጽራ እስትያ ‘and not … her, my drinking’ (ይሜጽራ is unknown to me (?)); ወኢይረውያ እጽገባ: ይረውያ is the simple stem of ረወየ ‘drink one’s fill’ (the verb of ኢረወይክዎ above; 3ms + -ኣ ‘her’), not a causative, so ‘and let not … have his fill of her, my being satisfied’ (?); ወኢይተፍኣ ‘and not spit her out’ (ተፍአ, ‘spit, vomit’ (?)). The syntax is loose and the English is a hedged reconstruction (?). The thought is that the satiety of wisdom never cloys.

sentences.t: ሰከርኩ ፡ ባቲ ፡ ወኢተንተንኩ ፡ ተንተንኩ ፡ በእንቲ ፡ አሃ ፡ ወኢወደቁ ፡ ወደቁ ፡ በእንቲአሃ ፡ ወኢተሀጐልኩ ፡ ባቲ ።
sentences.l: I-became-drunk in-her and-not I-staggered; I-staggered for-the-sake-of-her (አሃ); and-not they-fell; they-fell on-her-account; and-not I-was-lost in-her.
sentences.i: I was drunk with her, yet I did not stagger; I staggered for her sake, and they did not fall; they fell on her account; and I was not lost through her.
sentences.n: A string of paradoxes: ‘I did not stagger — I staggered’, ‘they did not fall — they fell’; the sense appears to be that she (wisdom) does not make the seeker fall in the way drink does, yet the seeker bears every hardship for her sake. ሰከርኩ ‘I became drunk’; ተንተንኩ ‘I staggered’ (the verb of ይተንትን in the petitions above); ወደቁ ‘they fell’ is a plural verb with no stated subject. በእንቲ ፡ አሃ is printed with a space; it is በእንቲአሃ ‘for her sake’ (as in the next unit), kept as printed.

sentences.t: ተሰጠምኩ ፡ በእንቲአሃ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ዐቢይ ፡ ባሕር ፡ ወአኀዝኩ ፡ ባሕርየ ፡ በውስተ ፡ ልጐተ ፡ መዓምቅቲሃ ፡ በዘባቲ ፡ እብዕል ፤
sentences.l: I-sank for-her-sake into great sea, and-I-took-hold pearl (?) in-within ልጐተ-of her-depths, in-that-which-in-her I-grow-rich;
sentences.i: For her sake I sank into the great sea, and I seized a pearl (?) in the ልጐተ (?) of its depths, that by what is in it I might be rich;
sentences.n: Here the sea-diving image begins, and it runs to the entry into the sun’s flame. ተሰጠምኩ ‘I sank’ (ሰጠመ, 1cs perfect, as in ይሰጠም). ባሕር ‘sea’; its depths are መዓምቅቲሃ, ‘her depths’, since ባሕር is treated as feminine (the ሃ cannot be wisdom here). ወአኀዝኩ ባሕርየ: ባሕርየ I take as the accusative of ባሕርይ ‘pearl’ (also ‘nature’; a pearl fits a diver and the wealth that follows) (?); the plain alternative is ባሕር + -የ ‘my sea’ (?). ልጐተ I cannot read; it follows በውስተ and precedes ‘her depths’, perhaps ‘bed, floor, ooze’ (?). በዘባቲ እብዕል ‘in what is in her I become rich’ (ዘ- relative, ባቲ ‘in her’, እብዕል 1cs imperfect, ባዕለ ‘be rich’). The treasures of wisdom are the pearls.

sentences.t: ወረድኩ ፡ ከመ ፡ ዐቢይ ፡ መልሕቀ ፡ ኀጺን ፡ በዘ ፡ ይበይታ ፡ አሕማር ፡ ውስተ ፡ ዕመቀ ፡ ባሕር ፡ ወነሣእኩ ፡ ማኅቶተ ፡ እንተ ፡ ታበርህ ፡ ሊተ ፡ ወዐረጉ ፡ በአሕባለ ፡ ራግናቲሃ ፡ ለልቡና ፤
sentences.l: And-I-went-down like great anchor-of iron in-which it-lodges-her (?) ships into depth-of sea, and-I-took lamp which she-shines to-me, and-they-ascended by-cords-of her-ራግና of-understanding;
sentences.i: And I went down like a great anchor of iron by which ships are moored (?), into the depth of the sea, and I took a lamp that shines for me, and they went up by the cords of its ራግና (?), those of understanding;
sentences.n: ወረድኩ ‘I went down’ (ወረደ). ዐቢይ መልሕቀ ኀጺን ‘a great anchor of iron’ (መልሕቅ ‘anchor’; ኀጺን in the construct). በዘ ይበይታ አሕማር: ይበይታ is the simple stem (not a causative) of በየተ ‘pass the night, lodge’ (?), 3ms + -ኣ ‘her’, the suffix unexplained; I read ‘by which ships are moored’ (?). አሕማር is plural, ‘ships’ (ሐመር), not the ‘red’ of an earlier gloss. ዕመቀ ባሕር ‘the depth of the sea’. ማኅቶተ እንተ ታበርህ ሊተ ‘a lamp which shines for me’ (the same verb አብርሀ as in ‘wisdom shines’ above, so the lamp is the light of wisdom). ወዐረጉ ‘and they went up’ (ዐረገ), plural with no stated subject, perhaps the pearls or the divers (?). አሕባለ ራግናቲሃ ለልቡና: አሕባል are ‘cords, ropes’ (construct); ራግናቲሃ ‘her ራግና’ I cannot read (?); ለልቡና ‘of understanding’ names whose cords they are.

sentences.t: ኖምኩ ፡ ውስተ ፡ መዓምቅቲሃ ፡ ለባሕር ፡ ወዘእንበለ ፡ እትዐዘዝ ፡ በማይ ፡ ሐለምኩ ፡ ባቲ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ኮከብ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሕፅንየ ፡ ወአንከርኩ ፡ ባቲ ፡ በእኂዞታ ፡ ወአጽናዕክዋ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ጸዳለ ፡ ፀሐይ ፡ አኀዝክዋ ፡ ወኢየኀድጋ ፡ እስከ ፡ ለዓለም ፤
sentences.l: I-slept in-her-depths of-the-sea and-without that-I-be-oppressed (?) by-water I-dreamed in-her, while star in my-bosom; and-I-marvelled in-her in-my-holding-her, and-I-made-firm-her with radiance-of sun; I-held-her and-not he-leaves-her until for-ever;
sentences.i: I slept in the depths of the sea, and without being oppressed (?) by the water I dreamed in her, with a star in my bosom; and I marvelled at her as I held her, and I made her firm with the radiance of the sun; I held her, and I will not leave her for ever;
sentences.n: ኖምኩ ‘I slept’; ሐለምኩ ‘I dreamed’ (ሐለመ), a dream in the depths, perhaps the vision of wisdom. ዘእንበለ እትዐዘዝ በማይ ‘without that I be … by water’: ዘእንበለ + the 1cs subjunctive of ተዐዘዘ ‘be oppressed, afflicted’ (?). እንዘ ኮከብ ውስተ ሕፅንየ ‘while a star (was) in my bosom’ (ሕፅን ‘bosom, lap’). በእኂዞታ ‘in holding her’ (አኀዘ, verbal noun with ‘her’). ወአጽናዕክዋ ‘and I made her firm’ (causative ጸንዐ), then አኀዝክዋ ‘I held her’. ወኢየኀድጋ ‘and not he leaves her’ is 3ms again, though the sense is ‘I’ (as in the petitions). ‘Her’ shifts between the sea, the lamp and wisdom; the Geʿez does not mark it, and I keep ‘her’ throughout. For ለዓለም ‘for ever’, compare ch. 87.

sentences.t: ቦእኩ ፡ ውስተ ፡ አናቅጸ ፡ መዛግብቲሃ ፡ ለጥበብ ፡ ወሔብኩ ፡ ሊተ ፡ ማየ ፡ አእምሮ ፤
sentences.l: I-entered into gates-of her-treasuries of-wisdom, and-ሔብኩ (?) to-me water-of knowledge;
sentences.i: I entered the gates of the treasuries of wisdom, and I drew (?) for myself the water of knowledge;
sentences.n: ቦእኩ ‘I entered’ (ቦአ, 1cs perfect), in this and the next unit. አናቅጸ መዛግብቲሃ ለጥበብ ‘gates of her treasuries, of wisdom’: the ለ- repeats the owner after the suffix, the usual doubling (compare ሕጉ ለእግዚኣብሔር). ወሔብኩ ሊተ: ሔብኩ I cannot place (it looks like a 1cs perfect of an unattested ሔበ; possibly a slip for ወሀብኩ ‘I gave’ or ሐበ ‘draw (water)’ (?)); ሊተ ‘to me, for myself’ and the object ማየ አእምሮ ‘water of knowledge’ suggest ‘drew’, which I give with a question mark. This answers the earlier line of the speech, where she says she has not yet drunk her fill of that water (in the ‘water of knowledge’ unit).

sentences.t: ቦእኩ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ዋዕየ ፡ ነበልባለ ፡ ፀሐይ ፡ ወአብርሀተኒ ፡ በጸዳላ ፡ ወተወልተውኩ ፡ ባቲ ፡ ወድኅንኩ ፡ በተወክሎታ ፤
sentences.l: I-entered into heat-of flame-of sun and-she-made-me-shine with-her-radiance, and-I-gleamed (?) in-her, and-I-was-saved by-trust-in-her;
sentences.i: I entered the heat of the flame of the sun, and she made me shine with her radiance, and I gleamed (?) in her, and I was saved by trusting in her;
sentences.n: ዋዕየ ነበልባለ ፀሐይ ‘heat of the flame of the sun’ (two constructs); the burning heat of the ‘water of knowledge’ unit returns, now as the light of wisdom, not a hardship. ወአብርሀተኒ ‘and she made me shine’ (አብርሀ, 3fs perfect + -ኒ ‘me’), with ጸዳላ ‘her radiance’. ወተወልተውኩ I read as ‘I gleamed/flashed’ (?), from a quadriliteral ወልተወ that I cannot confirm. ወድኅንኩ ‘and I was saved’ (ድኅነ); በተወክሎታ ‘by reliance on her’ (ተወክሎት, verbal noun of ተወክለ ‘trust’).

sentences.t: አኮ ፡ ሊተ ፡ ባሕቲትየ ፡ አላ ፡ ለኵሎሙ ፡ እለ ፡ ሖሩ ፡ በአሠራ ፡ ለጥበብ ፡ አኮ ፡ ሊተ ፡ ለባሕቲትየ ፡ አላ ፡ ለኵሎሙ ፡ ሰብአ ፡ ሀገርየ ፡ መንግሥተ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ ወአኮ ፡ ሎሙ ፡ ለባሕቲቶሙ ፡ አላ ፡ ለእለ ፡ የሐውሩ ፡ በፍኖቶሙ ፡ አሕዛብ ፡ እለ ፡ ዐውዶ ፡ ሙ ።
sentences.l: Not to-me alone-of-me but to-all-of-them who they-went in-footsteps-of-her of-wisdom; not to-me for-my-aloneness but to-all-of-them men-of my-country kingdom-of Ethiopia; and-not to-them for-their-aloneness but to-those who they-go in-their-way, nations who around-them (ዐውዶ ሙ).
sentences.i: Not for me alone, but for all who have gone in the footsteps of wisdom; not for me alone, but for all the people of my country, the kingdom of Ethiopia; and not for them alone, but for those who walk in their way, the nations that are around them.
sentences.n: A threefold widening of the benefit: ሊተ ባሕቲትየ ‘to me, my aloneness’ (ባሕቲት ‘alone’, with suffix) → ሰብአ ሀገርየ መንግሥተ ኢትዮጵያ ‘men of my land, the kingdom of Ethiopia’ (ሰብአ and መንግሥተ in the construct) → the neighbouring nations (አሕዛብ). በአሠራ ለጥበብ ‘in her footprints, of wisdom’ (አሠር ‘track, footprint’; the ለ- doubles the owner again). ባሕቲቶሙ ‘their aloneness’. The last words are printed እለ ፡ ዐውዶ ፡ ሙ, with a stray space: it is እለ ዐውዶሙ ‘those who (are) around them’ (ዐውድ ‘circuit, surroundings’ + -ሙ), kept as printed. ‘Nations’ may mean the peoples around Ethiopia, or the Gentiles at large.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወሀበነ ፡ ዘርአ ፡ በጽዮን ፡ ወማኅደረ ፡ በኢየሩሳሌም ፡ ወዓዲ ፡ ኮነ ፡ ክፍለ ፡ ምስለ ፡ እለ ፡ ኀረየ ፡ ዘርአ ፡ ያዕቆብ ፡ እስመ ፡ ረሰያ ፡ ለማኅደሩ ፡ ትኅድር ፡ ምስሌነ ፤
sentences.l: For God gave-us seed in-Zion and-dwelling-place in-Jerusalem, and-moreover he-became portion with those who he-chose seed-of Jacob, for he-made-her to-his-dwelling-place she-dwells with-us;
sentences.i: For God gave us a seed in Zion and a dwelling-place in Jerusalem, and moreover he became a portion (?) with those whom he chose, the seed of Jacob, for he made her, his dwelling-place, dwell with us;
sentences.n: ወሀበነ ‘he gave us’ (ወሀበ + -ነ). ዘርአ በጽዮን ‘seed in Zion’ and ማኅደረ በኢየሩሳሌም ‘dwelling in Jerusalem’: the Israelite lineage and the seat of God, in the claim of the book now passed to Ethiopia. ወዓዲ ኮነ ክፍለ: ‘and moreover he/it became a portion’ (?); ኮነ may stand for ኮንነ ‘we became’, as the published entry for this form notes elsewhere, which would give ‘we became a portion with those whom he chose’ (?). The portion language recalls Jeremiah 10:16 and Deuteronomy 32:9, ‘the Lord’s portion is his people, Jacob’, and I leave the subject open (?). ኀረየ ‘he chose’; ዘርአ ያዕቆብ ‘seed of Jacob’. ረሰያ ለማኅደሩ ትኅድር ምስሌነ: ‘he made her, his dwelling-place, dwell with us’; ረሰየ + -ያ ‘her’ is doubled by ለማኅደሩ (the dwelling = Zion, i.e. the Ark; ትኅድር 3fs imperfect).

sentences.t: እሙንቱሰ ፡ እምይእዜ ፡ ተዐቅጹ ፡ ወንሕነሰ ፡ እምይእዜ ፡ ረታዕነ ፡ እሙንቱሰ ፡ እምይእዜ ፡ ኀስሩ ፡ ወተመነኑ ፡ ወንሕነሰ ፡ እምይእዜ ፡ ከበርነ ፡ ወተፈቀርነ ፡ እስከ ፡ ለዓለመ ፡ ዓለም ፡ ወለትውልደ ፡ ትውልድ ፡ ዘይመጽእ ።
sentences.l: They-indeed from-now they-have-been-shut-in (?) and-we-indeed from-now we-have-been-upright (?); they-indeed from-now they-have-been-diminished and-they-have-been-despised, and-we-indeed from-now we-have-been-honoured and-we-have-been-loved until for-age-of age and-for-generation-of generation which-comes.
sentences.i: They, from now on, are shut in (?), and we, from now on, are upright (?); they, from now on, are diminished and despised, and we, from now on, are honoured and loved, for ever and ever, and for every generation to come.
sentences.n: Two pairs set in balance with the contrastive -ሰ: እሙንቱሰ ‘they, for their part’ and ወንሕነሰ ‘and we, for our part’, each followed by እምይእዜ ‘from now’. ‘They’ are the other peoples, or those who rejected Zion; I do not claim to know which. ተዐቅጹ is a tä-stem 3mp perfect I take as ‘were shut in/constrained’ (?); ረታዕነ is the simple stem, 1cp perfect, of ረትዐ ‘be straight, right’ (intransitive, so ‘we are upright, in the right’, not ‘were made upright’) (?). ኀስሩ ‘they were diminished’ (ኀሠረ, spelled with ስ) and ተመነኑ ‘they were despised’ are both perfects, contrasted with ከበርነ ‘we have been honoured’ (ከበረ) and ተፈቀርነ ‘we have been loved’ (tä-stem passive of ፈቀረ ‘love’). እስከ ለዓለመ ዓለም ‘until for the age of the age’ is the common ‘for ever and ever’; ለትውልደ ትውልድ ዘይመጽእ ‘for the generation of the generation that comes’ (ዓለም and ትውልድ doubled in construct).

sentences.t: ወአንትሙኒ ፡ መኳንንት ፡ ስምዑኒ ፡ ወጠይቅዋ ፡ ለመክሥተ ፡ አፉየ ፡ ወቃልየ ፤
sentences.l: And-you-also nobles hear-me and-examine-it the-opening-of my-mouth and-my-word;
sentences.i: And you also, nobles, hear me, and examine what my mouth opens and my word;
sentences.n: ወአንትሙኒ ‘and you also’ (the enclitic -ኒ) turns to the Israelite lords (መኳንንት ‘nobles, governors’). ስምዑኒ ‘hear me’ (imperative + -ኒ). ወጠይቅዋ ለመክሥተ አፉየ ወቃልየ: ‘and examine it, the opening of my mouth and my word’; -ዋ ‘it’ anticipates the object, and መክሥት (verbal noun of ከሠተ ‘open’) in the construct, ‘the opening of my mouth’, means her utterance. Lexical hedge on ጠየቀ ‘examine, investigate’ (?).

sentences.t: አፍቅርዋ ፡ ለርትዕ ፡ ወጽልእዋ ፡ ለሐሰት ፡ ርትዕሰ ፡ ጽድቅ ፡ ወሐሰትሰ ፡ ርእሰ ፡ ዐመፃ ፡ ወኢትትዓመፁ ፡ በበይናቲክሙ ፤
sentences.l: Love-it justice and-hate-it falsehood; justice-indeed righteousness and-falsehood-indeed head-of wrong, and-not do-wrong among-yourselves;
sentences.i: Love justice and hate falsehood; justice is righteousness, and falsehood is the head of wrongdoing; and do not wrong one another;
sentences.n: Two imperatives, አፍቅርዋ ‘love’ and ወጽልእዋ ‘hate’, each with -ዋ ‘it’ anticipating the object (ለርትዕ, ለሐሰት ‘justice’, ‘falsehood’). ርትዕ (‘straightness, justice’) is glossed by ጽድቅ ‘righteousness’; ሐሰት (‘lie’) by ርእሰ ዐመፃ ‘head of wrong’ (ርእስ in the construct, ‘source, chief’), the two -ሰ giving a neat contrast. ወኢትትዓመፁ ‘and do not do wrong’ (tä-stem, 2mp). በበይናቲክሙ ‘among yourselves’ (?). The ch. 88 charge to the son also centres on justice.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ የኀድር ፡ ምስሌክሙ ፡ ወማኅደረ ፡ ስብሐቲሁ ፡ ማእከሌክሙ ፡ እስመ ፡ ሰብአ ፡ ቤቱ ፡ ኮንክሙ ፡ ወኅድጉ ፡ እምይእዜ ፡ ዘትካት ፡ ልማድክሙ ፡ ተጠይሮ ፡ ወአጣዕዎ ፡ ሰገለ ፡ ወሥራየ ፡ ወቀስመ ፡ ወሐረሰ ፤
sentences.l: for God he-dwells with-you and-dwelling-of his-glory among-you, for men-of his-house you-became; and-abandon from-now former (?) your-custom: ተጠይሮ (?) and-አጣዕዎ (?), ሰገለ (?) and-ሥራየ (?) and-ቀስመ (?) and-ሐረሰ (?);
sentences.i: for God dwells with you, and the dwelling-place of his glory is among you, for you have become people of his house; and from now on give up your former (?) custom: ተጠይሮ (?) and idolatry (?), sorcery (?) and spells (?) and divination (?) and ሐረሰ (?);
sentences.n: የኀድር ‘he dwells’ (ኀደረ), ምስሌክሙ ‘with you’, ማእከሌክሙ ‘in your midst’. ወማኅደረ ስብሐቲሁ ‘and the dwelling-of his glory’: a construct chain again, ‘glory’ being the Divine Presence in the Ark. ሰብአ ቤቱ ኮንክሙ ‘you have become men of his house’. ወኅድጉ ‘and leave off, abandon’ (ኀደገ, imperative). ዘትካት ልማድክሙ: ‘your former custom’ (ትካት ‘formerly’ (?); the published entry also allows ‘your established custom’, from ተከለ ‘plant, establish’; ልማድ ‘custom, habit’), the old pagan practices of the Ethiopians. The list is the one of chs. 87 and 60b: ተጠይሮ is unknown (?), ወአጣዕዎ ‘idolatry’ from ጣዖት ‘idol’ (?), ሰገለ is ሰገል ‘sorcery’ (?) as in those chapters, ወሥራየ ‘and spells, magic’ (ሥራይ) (?), ወቀስመ I take as ቀሰመ ‘divine’ (cf. መቃስም ‘diviners’, ch. 60b) (?), and ሐረሰ is unclear to me (?). The Geʿez has no ‘and’ before ተጠይሮ or ሰገለ, which I keep.

sentences.t: ወለእመቦ ፡ ዘተረክበ ፡ እምዮም ፡ በውስተ ፡ ዘትካት ፡ ልማድ ፡ ይትበርበር ፡ ቤቱ ፡ ወይትኰነን ፡ ምስለ ፡ ብእሲቱ ፡ ወውሉዲ ፡ ወንዋዩ ፨
sentences.l: And-if-there-is who he-was-found from-today in-within former custom, he-is-plundered his-house and-he-is-condemned with his-wife and-ውሉዲ and-his-goods.
sentences.i: And if anyone is found from today in the former custom, his house shall be plundered, and he shall be condemned, with his wife and his children (?) and his goods.
sentences.n: ወለእመቦ ‘and if there is (anyone)’ (ለእመ ‘if’ + ቦ ‘there is’). ዘተረክበ ‘who is found’ (ዘ- + passive ተረክበ), እምዮም ‘from today’. ይትበርበር ቤቱ ‘his house is plundered’ (ተበርበረ, a quadriliteral tä-stem passive, imperfect, with the subject after it); ወይትኰነን ‘and he is condemned’ (ተኰነነ ‘be judged, condemned’). ወውሉዲ is printed so (ውሉድ with -ዲ?); I take it as ውሉዱ ‘his children’ with the last sign a slip (?), kept as printed. ንዋዩ ‘his goods’. The unit ends in ፨, which marks the end of the speech to the lords.

sentences.t: ወትቤሎ ፡ ለአዛርያስ ፡ በል ፡ ንግር ፡ ዘከመ ፡ ታፈቅር ፡ እግዝእትነ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ሰማያዊ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: And-said-she-to-him to-Azariah: say! tell how she-loves our-lady with king heavenly. ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.i: And she said to Azariah, ‘Say on! Tell how our lady loves with the heavenly king (?).’
sentences.n: ወትቤሎ ‘and she said to him’ (ትቤ + ሎ), the queen addressing Azariah (the Azariah of ch. 88, written Azaryas in the Geʿez). Two imperatives, በል ‘say!’ and ንግር ‘tell!’ (the second of ነገረ). ዘከመ ‘how’; ታፈቅር is the 3fs imperfect of አፍቀረ ‘love’ (the verb has no simple stem in use); ምስለ ንጉሥ ሰማያዊ is ‘with the heavenly king’, so ‘loves with’ means ‘is in loving union with’ (?). እግዝእትነ ‘our lady’ is Zion, as in ch. 88. This is the command that opens the next speech. The six ፨ at the end close the chapter, as the ፨ marks do in the source.
